title: Book Three · Chapter 114: The Room on the Page
story:
In the sixth week of term, Anna brings a drawing to lunch.

It shows one long room. There are windows on one side and a door near a corner.

“A classroom?” Ronan asks.

“A reading room. For the drawing lesson.”

She puts six small paper shapes on it. Each shape is a table. Ronan watches her move them between the door and the windows.

“Can I try?”

She gives him two.

He puts both beside the windows. Then he moves a third table close to them.

Anna points at the narrow space.

“How does that person get out?”

Ronan looks at the middle table. He moves his finger along the edge and stops.

“Through the window.”

Anna laughs. “Try the door first.”

He pulls the middle table back. Now there is a clear path behind the chairs.

“Better?”

She tries the path with her own finger.

“Better.”

They move the last two tables. One place stays close to the light. Another has more room for a large bag.

Ronan looks up at their classroom. A boy is moving sideways behind two chairs. He is carrying his lunch with both hands.

“Our room needs your paper tables.”

“Our room needs smaller bags.”

Anna moves her own bag under her chair. Ronan follows her example.

The boy with the lunch reaches their row. He stops behind the chair at the next desk. His bowl is too full to hold sideways.

Anna pulls her own chair in. Ronan moves his feet. The boy passes and thanks them. Nothing spills.

Ronan looks down at the six paper tables.

“We forgot the bowls.”

“We need room for people and their bowls,” Anna says.

She moves one paper table a little farther from the door. Then she draws a wider path around its corner. This time, Ronan leaves the shape where she puts it.

After lunch, she takes the drawing to the school library. Ronan goes with her to return a book.

There is a folder of course information near the desk. The teacher showed Anna the folder that morning.

She opens the part about building design. Some pages describe short lessons. Others describe years of study in another city.

Anna reads one page twice. Then she copies an address.

“You want that one?” Ronan asks.

“I want more information first.”

She shows him the little picture at the top. It has rooms, doors, and people beside a building.

“I like this work,” she says. “The maths matters. But people need to use the rooms too.”

Ronan thinks of the boy with his lunch.

“And get out again.”

“Usually.”

She smiles and shuts the folder. The address goes into her notebook beside the room plan.

At the desk, Ronan returns his book. Anna asks the librarian about the course page. The librarian finds an envelope for her request.

Ronan waits beside the shelves. When Anna comes back, she has the envelope and the paper tables in her hand.

One table has stuck to her sleeve. He points to it.

“A very small customer.”

She takes it off carefully and puts it with the others. Then they carry the room back to class.
studyGuide:
## 词句提示

shape＝形状、纸形；path＝通路；folder＝文件夹；building design＝建筑设计。

## 理解问题

1. Ronan第一次放桌子时出了什么实际问题？他怎样改动？
2. Anna抄地址是已经选定学校了吗？她想进一步了解什么？

## 读句子

**Now there is a clear path behind the chairs.**

拆开看：Now / there is / a clear path / behind the chairs.

现在／有了／一条畅通的路／在椅子后方。
